result_text:
I fixed `--sort-reexports` in `isort/core.py`. A multi-line `__all__` after reformatted imports is now sorted in place instead of corrupting the file.

The old code worked out where `__all__` starts in the output by adding up the lengths of the input lines. That position was wrong whenever isort changed the earlier text, for example by collapsing the multi-line `from mylib import (...)` onto one line. The sorted `__all__` was then written at the wrong place and overwrote part of the imports (`fro__all__`). I now read the actual output position once the `__all__` line has been written, and use that.

I ran your case with a leading comment added. It now gives `__all__ = ('func1', 'func2')` after `from mylib import module1, module2`, with nothing mangled. `tests/unit/test_isort.py` and `tests/unit/test_regressions.py` pass (285 passed, 1 skipped). I didn't add a test for this case, as you asked.

I didn't get a run of the whole test suite. When I tried a filtered run over `tests/unit`, 8 files failed during collection, so nothing ran from that run. I didn't look into why.
